Who is responsible?

Boarding Time is developed by Stephen Curtis, an individual developer. For privacy questions or requests, email stephencurtisapps@gmail.com.

This policy covers the app, support correspondence and this website. It describes the current local-first app; platform services and external providers have their own practices.

Calendar permission and information

Boarding Time asks for full calendar event access because iOS does not offer a read-only permission for reading events. Full access technically permits reading and writing; Boarding Time uses it to read and display events and does not create, edit, save or delete calendar events.

The app reads event titles, start and end dates/times, occurrence identifiers, all-day status, location text, notes and calendar names, identifiers and source labels. It also reads calendar type and subscription status. Event location text is not your device’s GPS location. The app does not request Contacts, Reminders or device location access.

For a requested date, the app queries accessible calendars and applies display choices afterwards. Selecting or hiding a calendar in Boarding Time controls presentation, not the extent of the calendar permission. Opening an event can show additional details through Apple’s native event viewer, with editing disabled.

What stays on your device

Event details are processed in memory; Boarding Time does not maintain its own persistent event database. It saves calendar configuration locally, including identifiers, last-known names and source labels, custom line labels, colours, ordering, visibility and selection preferences. Those labels may contain personal information.

Appearance, theme, board style and Date Line preferences, and a flag recording whether calendar access was previously granted, are also stored locally. iOS manages the selected app icon. Saved settings remain across ordinary app updates and can include calendars that later become unavailable.

Developer collection and tracking

The app has no developer-operated backend, advertising, tracking or integrated third-party analytics or crash-reporting SDK. It does not send calendar information to Stephen Curtis or operate an app-managed cloud sync service. You do not need a Boarding Time account.

Apple may process platform diagnostics and TestFlight information according to its services and your choices. Feedback, screenshots, attachments or diagnostics you submit through Apple’s feedback services may be made available to Stephen Curtis. Such submissions are separate from the app’s local processing; Boarding Time does not automatically upload calendar events to the developer. Calendar providers may synchronise your calendars independently.

Permissions, retention and deletion

You can withdraw calendar permission in iOS or iPadOS Settings. When Boarding Time rechecks permission, it stops calendar access and clears its verified event snapshot. Revoking permission does not remove saved calendar names, source labels or preferences. Ending the app process releases its in-memory event state; this is not a secure-memory-erasure guarantee.

There is no in-app erase-all control. Deleting the app removes its local app container; offloading keeps its data. Neither action deletes your system calendar events or necessarily deletes existing device backups or support correspondence.

Device security and backups

Local information relies on the device’s app sandbox and platform security. Boarding Time does not add separate encryption to its settings file or exclude it from backups. Device or computer backups may contain app settings and calendar metadata, depending on your configuration. Backup restoration can restore this information.

Protect your device and backups. Information visible on screen may also appear in screenshots or system app-switcher previews. No method of storage or transmission can be guaranteed completely secure.

If you contact support

Support is personally managed by Stephen Curtis using Gmail. If you email support, Stephen receives your email address, any name you provide, your message and attachments. This information is used to answer your request, investigate and resolve the issue, and follow up with you. It is not used for marketing or advertising. Contacting support is optional and does not affect access to the app.

Please provide only information needed to explain the problem. Redact event titles, calendar names, notes and other personal details from screenshots, and avoid sending sensitive information or information about other people unless necessary.

The lawful basis for ordinary support correspondence is legitimate interests: answering voluntary requests and resolving problems with Boarding Time. The documented assessment considers the limited information needed, your reasonable expectations and safeguards such as minimisation and retention limits. This basis does not automatically authorise unrelated uses or processing of sensitive information.

Your right to object: you can object to support processing based on legitimate interests by emailing stephencurtisapps@gmail.com. Your request will be considered in accordance with applicable law.

Routine support correspondence is permanently deleted from accessible mailbox locations within 12 months of issue resolution, including relevant Sent, archived and Trash copies. Unnecessary sensitive material should be removed earlier. Provider backup retention may extend beyond this deletion. If particular information must be kept for a legal obligation or legal claim, retention is limited to what is necessary for that purpose.

If you submit feedback, screenshots, attachments or diagnostics through Apple’s platform services and those are made available to the developer, Stephen may receive and use them to investigate and respond to the issue. They may contain personal information. They are separate from data processed locally by the app. Copies retained by Stephen for routine support are subject to the support retention arrangements above; Apple controls retention within its own services.

Google and other email providers involved in delivery process correspondence to operate and protect their services. Gmail can use automated processing for features and security. Google describes international processing and publishes information about its transfer arrangements in its privacy policy and data-transfer information. Information may be processed outside the UK. This policy does not promise UK-only storage, end-to-end encryption or immediate deletion of provider backups.

Website hosting and external links

This site is prepared for hosting on GitHub Pages. No analytics scripts, advertising, embedded third-party media, external fonts or site-set cookies are included. GitHub states that Pages logs visitor IP addresses for security. GitHub describes processing in the United States and other countries and explains its international-transfer arrangements. This hosting activity is separate from calendar processing in Boarding Time. No fixed host-log retention period or UK-only hosting is promised here. See GitHub’s privacy statement.

Links to external websites make requests only when you choose to follow them. Email links open your chosen email service; this website does not submit a support form.

Your UK privacy rights

For personal information held for support, you may have rights of access, correction, erasure, restriction, objection and portability, depending on the circumstances and applicable lawful basis. In particular, you can object to processing based on legitimate interests. Contact the email above to exercise your rights; a request does not guarantee deletion of records that must lawfully be retained.

You can complain to the UK Information Commissioner’s Office at ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint. The developer cannot retrieve or erase calendar information held only on your device; manage calendar permissions, device data and backups through their respective settings.

Children and policy changes

Boarding Time has no account or age-verification system and is not designed to collect children’s personal information through a backend. If a child sends a support message, the correspondence may contain personal information; contact the developer about any concern.

This policy will be updated if the app or support practices change. A published version will state its effective or updated date. This document is an unpublished draft reviewed on 28 October 2026.
